newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - British Gas options busy as shares weaken.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - British Gas options busy as shares weaken.

text.p: British Gas traded options were busy on Thursday following news that the company had opted for another monopolies and merger commission inquiry concerning price controls for its gas transmission business.
Expecting the underlying shares to weaken, one of the biggest deals was from a buyer of 1,500 December 200 puts at prices of 13p and 14p, dealers said.
There was also a seller of 1,000 December 200 calls at 3p and a seller of 800 March 200 puts at 15-1/2p.
British Gas shares fell back 5-1/2p to 194p.

In contrast, a bullish deal in shipping and transportion group P&O may have been prompted by news that the company would merge its short-sea ferry business on the English Channel with Stena Line AB of Sweden.
The news triggered the purchase of 2,500 November 700 calls in P&O at prices of 7p and 8p. Another trader bought 400 November 650 calls at prices ranging from 23p to 30p.
Options interest was also generated in Imperial Tobacco where bid speculation for the group was dismissed by the company.
The main deal was a synthetic long position established by buying 1,000 February 420 calls at 35p and selling 1,000 February 420 puts at at 18p.
The shares added 16-1/2p to 420-1/2p and at the February expiry date the deal will make money if the shares go above 437.

Over in the FTSE 100 index options there was a flurry of trades from buyers of puts some of whom hedged their positions by buying December FTSE futures in volatility trades ahead of Friday's U.S. payroll data.
At 1415 GMT, the FTSE index was down 12.7 at 4002.4.
